relations.myth: The Wedding of Nikkal and Yarikh
relations.note: Yarikh courts Nikkal, refuses alternative brides, pays a bride-price, and marries her.

relations.myth: The Wedding of Nikkal and Yarikh
relations.note: Nikkal is his daughter; he negotiates her marriage and proposes alternative brides to Yarikh.
The collective birth and marriage goddesses participate in the poem's disputed nuptial and fertility conclusion.
Baal appears indirectly as father of alternative brides offered to Yarikh instead of Nikkal.
Pidray is apparently offered to Yarikh instead of Nikkal, but Yarikh refuses her.
Yabdaray is apparently offered to Yarikh instead of Nikkal, but Yarikh refuses her.
Nikkal is paired with the Hurrian moon god as his spouse in ritual traditions.
Hurrian sequences placing Umbu before Nikkal most plausibly designate them as a divine couple.
Nikkal belongs to Ḫepat's ordered offering circle without an asserted blood relationship.
At Ankuwa, Nikkal receives offerings within Teššub's circle rather than Ḫepat's.
Nikkal stands beside or follows Damkina in the ordered Yazılıkaya divine procession.
Nikkal is positioned before Aya in the ordered Yazılıkaya and ritual-list procession.
Nikkal receives offerings in a mixed ritual centered on Šauška and Ashtart.
Nikkal occurs in the offering sequence of a mixed ritual centered on Ashtart and Šauška.
Ninatta occurs after Nikkal in a ritual offering sequence associated with Šauška.
Kulitta occurs after Nikkal in a ritual offering sequence associated with Šauška.
As Ningal, Nikkal is the wife of the Mesopotamian moon god Nanna.
relations.source: Mesopotamian hymns, lists, and cult documents

relations.note: As Ningal, Nikkal is Utu's mother in standard Mesopotamian learned genealogy.
As Ningal, Nikkal is Inanna's mother in standard Mesopotamian learned genealogy.
The Egyptian healing spell calls Nikkal the wife of this foreign god, probably a moon deity.
Resheph follows the Upper God and Nikkal in an Egyptian healing invocation.
Adamma appears with Resheph in the formula adjacent to the Upper God and Nikkal.
